tests.label: Installed DEV build
tests.instructions: Confirm the installed TU version matches the target release. This checks only the visible version label.

tests.label: Ten integrated tools registered
tests.instructions: Read the shared TU API and confirm all ten expected tools are registered; Stock and Calculations must be absent. Registration does not prove a tool works.

tests.label: Temporary storage roundtrip
tests.instructions: Write, read and remove only a temporary TU Test key; do not touch tool data.

tests.label: Published single-script DEV artifact
tests.instructions: Check release metadata, ten bundled factory markers, removed tool exclusion and DEV-only backend URLs. This is a source check, not runtime validation.

tests.label: GitHub published agreement
tests.instructions: Read the small published DEV agreement version.json metadata file. Full agreement text is not fetched by this automatic check.

tests.label: DEV Worker published agreement
tests.instructions: Ask the authenticated TU Manager for a read-only DEV agreement-status check. Confirm its published version; the tool does not receive keys/tokens or download full text. If authentication is unavailable, mark BLOCKED.

tests.label: Agreement version consistency
tests.instructions: Compare the published agreement_version values only. Wording, number and effective-date fields are not compared for this verification. Full agreement remains available for user review in TU.

tests.label: Public Only registration
tests.instructions: In DEV, register using a Public Only key. Verify the server-confirmed access label and accepted current agreement. Record outcome only; never paste the key.

tests.label: Limited Access registration
tests.instructions: Repeat with a Limited Access key in DEV; verify its label and access to the features requiring that level.

tests.label: Reject unsupported or invalid keys
tests.instructions: Verify Full Access, unsupported levels and invalid keys are rejected with actionable errors and are not persisted.

tests.label: Saved keys and verified per-key labels
tests.instructions: Save at least two Public Only and two Limited Access keys. Verify each is listed once with its own Torn-verified access level and owner, even after reload. Adding a key must leave the current login unchanged. Recheck legacy keys; explicitly switch the login and War Organizer key, and verify other keys remain saved.

tests.label: Remove one key without losing others
tests.instructions: Remove an inactive key and verify every copy is removed while other keys and the login remain. Remove the active login in a dedicated DEV session: cancellation must be confirmed before deletion, other saved keys must remain, and the deleted key must not return after reload through GM or legacy storage. Cancellation/network failure must retain the active key.

tests.label: Show / Hide API key
tests.instructions: Check registration and Settings fields toggle between masked and visible values without exposing values in reports.

tests.label: Session and agreement persistence
tests.instructions: Accept the current agreement, navigate and reload Torn; authorization restores without another acceptance prompt. With a fresh session cache, verify no repeated key/profile or full agreement downloads. After the five-minute verification cache expires, confirm a metadata status check on activity/resume. Closing the host may require normal session restoration.

tests.label: Expired session renewal
tests.instructions: Use a controlled DEV session to verify expired tokens renew once through the Manager, backend revocation stops access, cross-tab logout clears cached access, and changed agreement versions require explicit acceptance. TU Test read-only version checking must never register or accept automatically.

tests.label: Authentication failure recovery
tests.instructions: Verify rejected/revoked keys, rate limits and network failures produce clear recovery steps without repeated requests or prompts.

tests.label: Complete published agreement
tests.instructions: Compare all displayed content plus version, number and effective date with the published DEV agreement.

tests.label: Agreement acceptance record
tests.instructions: After explicitly accepting in DEV, inspect an authorized backend response or event record confirming the acceptance event for the current agreement. Record the event type, agreement version and confirmation timestamp without credentials. Successful UI access alone does not pass this check; mark BLOCKED if backend evidence is unavailable. This tool never submits acceptance.

tests.label: Cancellation and revocation
tests.instructions: In a dedicated DEV session, cancel acceptance and confirm backend event/revocation, tool access removal and a subsequent valid recovery.

tests.label: Version-change reacceptance
tests.instructions: With an approved controlled DEV agreement update, verify old acceptance no longer grants access. Do not modify production or publish terms just to complete this checklist.

tests.label: Credentials stay private
tests.instructions: Inspect diagnostics, exported backups/reports and console output. Confirm no API keys, bearer tokens or room secrets appear; record no secret values.

tests.label: Tools / Settings / About
tests.instructions: Open each tab, Business Tools, Games single/multiplayer, Chat Tools and War Tools. War Organizer belongs under War Tools. No module installation/catalog controls or removed tools.

tests.label: Approved gold logo
tests.instructions: Check the approved no-flare Integrated Gold master in launcher, headers and War Organizer on standard/high-density displays. Check sharpness, proportions, transparent exterior and compact launcher size. About must not include a full-resolution logo link.

tests.label: Launcher visibility and dragging
tests.instructions: Drag with mouse and touch as applicable; reload to verify position persistence, keep launcher on-screen after rotation/resize. On PDA, verify early script injection waits for BODY, saved positions remain on-screen after restart and TU Test startup diagnostics report ready with a launcher present. For DEV 0.5.42.48, verify startup after PDA adaptSource quote normalization. Previous builds contained a curly apostrophe that could prevent parsing before any startup marker.

tests.label: Window navigation and layout
tests.instructions: Check Back, Minimize, Restore and Exit, drag/resize, saved positions, viewport bounds, stacking, scrolling and overflow.

tests.label: Lazy startup and cleanup
tests.instructions: With Manager and tools closed, verify no authorization polling interval, connected Manager DOM observers or background tool initialization. Opening a tool should initialize only that tool; Torn page-content observers should exist only for activated tools that need them. Repeat close/Exit/switch and verify observers/timers stop. Minimizing an active monitor may preserve its intended monitoring.

tests.label: Reload and duplicate injection
tests.instructions: Reload and test normal Torn SPA navigation; verify one launcher and one instance per tool with no startup exceptions.

tests.label: Native host / request bridges
tests.instructions: In the selected actual host, exercise its real GM legacy/modern or PDA/fetch bridge and isolated/shared page context. A mocked or desktop-browser result cannot prove PDA compatibility.

tests.label: Settings persistence
tests.instructions: Change time display and tool settings; reload and verify saved values and unaffected historical data.

tests.label: Backup and restoration
tests.instructions: Export TU-managed data and restore in a controlled DEV profile; verify additive restoration and key exclusion. Separately export/import large archives and legacy data using each tool.

tests.label: Single-script update
tests.instructions: Install/update via rolling DEV URL; confirm version, all ten tools, settings/history, approved logo, and no separate tool installation.

tests.label: Rollback procedure
tests.instructions: In a controlled DEV profile, disable the integrated script and restore the previous Manager/tools without clearing storage. Confirm recovery; then return to the target DEV build.

tests.label: Travel Assistant and Item Monitor — functional test
tests.instructions: Select/cancel items, manage watches, trigger quantity/price alerts, verify alarms and persistence. Exercise Travel planning, live DEV reporting, predictions and failure recovery on representative Torn pages. Complete List location labels must show only foreign country names, e.g. Canada; Torn Item Market/Bazaar remains available. Country filtering and selecting a Foreign monitor must retain their original meaning. Validate screen color alert below the filter: red while armed/waiting, green flashing with stock, and removed on cancel/return or disabling it. Inventory Destruction is OFF by default, requires explicit red-warning acceptance, targets foreign travel slots only, and adds a separate Destroy Travel Inventory click after optional Heal. Use a disposable test inventory only when deliberately validating destruction; check exact Trash/Yes, per-item removal evidence, partial failures and no automatic retries. Planning to Hospitalize Yes requires healing and hospitalization selections. Test Hospitalize Me with no stock, native item Use/Yes, confirmed hospital status, then wait for stock and Heal. Stock already present must skip hospitalization. Destruction must list and confirm selected item types only, preserving unselected items. Legacy all-item consent must not re-enable destruction. Select None — already used / skip hospitalization with a healing item, then arm while already hospitalized or while flight status is still Traveling. It must not demand another hospitalization item or offer Hospitalize Me. After stock appears, observed hospital status determines Heal versus the next step. While hospitalized and waiting for stock, confirm a second line shows remaining hospital seconds and decreases once per second. Flight arrival must not be used as hospital time. Unknown timing must be labeled unavailable, and timer expiry must never execute gameplay or infer release. Check countdown cleanup after stock arrives/cancel/exit. If Torn Max shows 17 while TU verifies 18, buy the shown 17 first. After confirmation and inventory update, at most one further purchase can use the verified remainder (for example 1). Never repeat the first batch. If stock/funds change or the follow-up is unconfirmed, retain the confirmed purchase, show the reconciliation warning and enable Return without another buy retry. While hospitalized verify + Hosp? with Hosp Time: MM:SS if selected hospitalization items remain; otherwise verify the time on Waiting for available stock. Test progressively faster blinking below the warning threshold, one hospital sound per deadline, and another sound after a confirmed extension. Each click must use one selected carried item; rapid taps while pending must not use additional items. Verify Purchase Max enters the calculated space/funds/stock maximum directly; native clamps may buy fewer first, with at most one confirmed remainder purchase. A stale consumed-item label must not block reconciliation. Check capacity-ledger, freed-slot and confirmed-purchase diagnostic fields.

tests.label: Travel Assistant and Item Monitor — lifecycle and saved data
tests.instructions: Open, minimize, restore, Back, Exit, switch away and reopen this tool repeatedly. Check viewport/scroll/touch behavior, one instance, saved data and cessation of polling/listeners after Exit. Verify no late errors or duplicate requests. Minimize the main monitor and planner, restore through the TU icon, and reopen the active tool through its Business Tools card repeatedly. Exactly one window must restore with unsaved input and an armed Snatch and Run intent preserved; no monitor restart/cancellation. Arm during an outbound foreign flight, refresh and wait over 15 minutes, confirm arrival enables fresh-stock actions and return flight hides the button. Check unknown identity during startup preserves intent and another player cannot use it. During the outbound flight with hospitalization planned, Hospitalize Me must ask confirmation naming the selected item. Decline uses nothing; confirmation verifies the same player/outbound destination and uses only native controls. Return flights, unavailable controls and repeated pending clicks must not cause a use or queued use at arrival.

tests.instructions: Use a Limited key to exercise faction roster, target/reservation controls, countdowns, refresh, historical data and API errors without automating attacks.

tests.label: Alarm preserves minimized window
tests.instructions: Minimize Travel Assistant with an active watch. Trigger an alarm while Torn is actively viewed; sound/status must update without restoring the main window. Restore manually and repeat; Exit stops monitoring.

tests.label: Show monitored items only
tests.instructions: Verify the checkbox sits beside Show monitored items only. On a foreign shop with unmonitored rows before monitored rows, enable it. Monitored items including zero-stock rows collect at the top of the item list with no empty slots; other entire item containers hide. Change watches and dynamic rows; disable or Exit restores all native rows in original order. Check native nested LI and table layouts.

tests.label: Snatch and Run eligibility and selection
tests.instructions: Verify domestic/in-flight states cannot arm. Abroad, select a monitored foreign item and answer hospital status. Hospital users select a labeled medical item with a Limited login. Arm: main window minimizes and exactly one red Snatch and Run button appears. Clicking red does nothing. No native-control selection buttons or floating status panel exist. Drag the red waiting button with touch/mouse and restore after reload; repeat while green. Moving/releasing must never heal, buy or travel. Check screen bounds after resize. While TU Test monitoring is active, export must include ordered Snatch and Run function events and native-step/error details; after Stop no function events are added. Select multiple healing and hospitalization types and refresh to verify persistence. Test the hospital warning threshold, audible alarm on/off, volume and beep/siren/chime. Verify the inventory overview shows total/used/free slots and each carried item type/count, with heal, hospitalization and accepted destruction annotations. Selected items must not free space until their action succeeds.

tests.label: Snatch and Run hospital release
tests.instructions: On actual PC Tampermonkey and Torn PDA separately: one green Heal click opens the exact selected inventory slot, selects Use and confirms Yes only for that item. Test Morphine and distinguish blood types. The native hospital-release result must enable Purchase Max without automatically buying. Test duplicate clicks, cancellation, lost focus, insufficient healing and stock disappearing before medical Yes.

tests.label: Snatch and Run Max and purchase confirmation
tests.instructions: On actual Torn PDA: one Purchase Max click opens the monitored buy icon, uses the visible quantity panel Max and Buy, waits for the item-specific Yes/No panel, validates exact quantity/item and selects Yes once. Hidden desktop fields must remain unused. Verify 17 purchased Dahlia plus a remaining medical item using selected-item inventory evidence. Retest the desktop inline controls, unrelated Yes dialogs, wrong item/quantity, missing capacity and cancellation. Also arm with No hospital, no medical selection and a saved name-based watch, using a Public Only key: resolve the exact visible native form/Buy item ID and buy without healing or an inventory API request. Verify newly selected watches retain native form IDs. Duplicate same-name rows and conflicting explicit IDs must block. After healing the last carried medical item, verify freshly free capacity is 18 and a stale native Max 17 is corrected to 18 when cash/stock permit. A remaining carried item must still occupy its slot. Verify insufficient funds and limited stock cap the quantity. The function timeline must show capacity-check values; no second purchase is submitted automatically.

tests.label: Snatch and Run return and cleanup
tests.instructions: On actual PC Tampermonkey and Torn PDA: after purchase proof, one Return click opens Travel home, verifies Torn in the native question, selects Travel Back, waits for booking proof, then selects enabled Continue. Confirm the flight screen, no duplicate booking and no automatic action on navigation/reload. Run continuous diagnostics before healing; stop/export only after safely on the flight. Fixture success does not pass live host acceptance. Test an existing empty/collapsed travel-home-panel and delayed rendering of its question. The action must expand Travel home once and wait for the Torn question/back control. If the native countdown automatically navigates to the flight screen, it must finish without an extra Continue click or timeout.
